source_text: Si quis dicat, partem duntaxat hominis assumpsisse Christum, et non confitetur ipsum per omnia similem nobis, excepto peccato; anathema esto. Quomodo potest quisquam dicere, partem tantummodo hominis assumpsisse Christum? cum ipse Dominus dicat: Animam meam pono, ut iterum eam accipiam, pro ovibus meis. Et caro mea vere est cibus, et sanguis meus vere est potus: et, qui manducat meam carnem, et bibit meum sanguinem habet vitam aeternam.
thought_title: Christ assumed the whole human being
orientation: Gregory anathematizes the claim that Christ assumed only part of a human, insisting he became like us in all things except sin, and supports this with Christ's own words about laying down his soul and giving his flesh and blood.
pass_a_gloss: If [anyone] says [that] [the] part only of man [was] assumed [by] Christ, and not [he] confesses [that] him [the] same through all [things] similar to us, except sin; anathema let him be. How [is he] able [anyone] to say, [the] part only of man [to have been] assumed [by] Christ? when [the] same Lord says: [My] soul I lay down, in order that again it I may receive, for [my] sheep. And [my] flesh truly is food, and [my] blood truly is drink: and, who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood [he] has life eternal.

choices.english: Christ assumed only a part of a human
choices.why: duntaxat restricts partem; accusative-infinitive construction after dicat.
rejected: Christ assumed a human part only
Christ took only part of a man

choices.form: per omnia similem nobis, excepto peccato
choices.english: like us in all things, except sin
choices.why: per omnia = in all respects; excepto peccato ablative absolute = except sin.
rejected: in every way like us, sin excepted

choices.why: Fixed formula of condemnation; glossary requires this exact phrasing.

choices.term: Animam meam pono, ut iterum eam accipiam, pro ovibus meis
choices.english: I lay down my soul, that I may take it again, for my sheep
choices.why: pono = lay down; accipiam = take again; pro ovibus meis = for my sheep; Christ speaking of his whole self.
rejected: I lay down my life, that I may take it again, for my sheep
I place my soul, to receive it back, for my sheep

choices.term: caro mea vere est cibus, et sanguis meus vere est potus
choices.english: my flesh truly is food, and my blood truly is drink
choices.why: vere = truly; cibus/potus = food/drink; Eucharistic realism matching glossary 'flesh'.
rejected: my flesh is truly food, and my blood is truly drink
my flesh is real food, and my blood real drink

pass_b_english: If anyone says that Christ assumed only a part of a human, and does not confess that he is like us in all things, except sin, let him be anathema. How can anyone say that Christ assumed only a part of a human? For the Lord himself says: I lay down my soul, that I may take it again, for my sheep. And my flesh truly is food, and my blood truly is drink: and whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life.
